message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends that occur in Canada during 2023**.  
These are the federal holidays that either fall on a weekend or are observed on a weekday, creating a three‑day (or longer) break that includes a weekend.  

| Long‑weekend period | Holiday(s) | Notes |
|---------------------|------------|-------|
| **Dec 31 2022 – Jan 2 2023** | New Year’s Day (observed on Jan 1) | New Year’s Day falls on Sunday, so the holiday is observed on the following Monday. |
| **Feb 18 – Feb 20 2023** | Family Day (Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario, etc.) | Observed on the third Monday of February. |
| **Apr 7 – Apr 9 2023** | Good Friday | Good Friday is a statutory holiday in all provinces. |
| **May 20 – May 22 2023** | Victoria Day | Celebrated on the Monday preceding May 25. |
| **Jul 1 – Jul 3 2023** | Canada Day (observed on Jul 1) | Canada Day falls on Saturday, so the holiday is observed on the preceding Friday. |
| **Sep 2 – Sep 4 2023** | Labour Day | Observed on the first Monday in September. |
| **Oct 7 – Oct 9 2023** | Thanksgiving | Observed on the second Monday in October. |
| **Nov 10 – Nov 12 2023** | Remembrance Day (observed on Nov 10) | Remembrance Day is a statutory holiday in many provinces; when it falls on a weekend it is observed on the preceding Friday. |
| **Dec 23 – Dec 25 2023** | Christmas Day | Christmas falls on Monday, so the long weekend runs from Saturday to Monday. |

### Things to keep in mind

| Province | Extra long‑weekends in 2023 |
|----------|-----------------------------|
| **Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario** | Family Day (Feb 20) |
| **Newfoundland & Labrador** | St. Patrick’s Day (Feb 17) – *not* a statutory holiday, but some businesses close. |
| **Quebec** | National Day for Truth and Reconciliation (Oct 28) – *not* a long weekend. |
| **Other provinces** | Some provinces observe **Remembrance Day** on Nov 10, creating the long weekend shown above. |

> **Tip for your app:**  
> If you need province‑specific data, you can pull the official holiday calendars from the Government of Canada’s “Public Holidays” page or from each provincial government’s website. The federal holidays listed above apply nationwide, but the exact dates for provincial holidays (e.g., Family Day, St. Patrick’s Day, National Day for Truth and Reconciliation) vary.

**Sources**

* Government of Canada – Public Holidays (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/finance/public-holidays.html)  
* Provincial government holiday calendars (e.g., Alberta: https://www.alberta.ca/public-holidays.aspx)

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the list broken down by province or if you need the dates in a different format!
